findings.title: Cached login IDP set is keyed by organizationId but ignores org-scoped invalidation
findings.body: The login query is cached per realm and FetchMode, with the organizationId as the searchKey. Invalidation only fires from IDP create/update/remove. Changes that alter results without touching the IDP, such as disabling an organization, deleting one, or changing org membership, do not invalidate the entry. The code relies on the isEnabled wrapper for the disabled-org case, but a deleted org or an IDP unlinked through the organization API may leave stale entries. In getByOrganization the code also checks isInvalid(orgId), and that check is missing here.

findings.title: update() invalidation uses the cached original, which may be stale or wrapped
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate compares the original (from getById, an org-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() depends on org state) with the updated model. The predicate is evaluated on the wrapper, so a disabled organization makes the original look like it is not a login IDP. As a result invalidation can be skipped or triggered wrongly. The comparison should use the raw stored model.

findings.title: remove() may NPE when the IDP does not exist
findings.body: storedIdp is now fetched unconditionally via idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias). When the alias is unknown it is null. registerIDPLoginInvalidation tolerates null through the predicate's nonNull check. However, in the isInvalid branch registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) dereferences it, which is the same as the old behavior. The unconditional extra DB lookup on every remove is also new.

findings.title: Per-id getById calls on every cached login lookup
findings.body: On a cache hit, each cached id is resolved via session.identityProviders().getById(id). Each miss there costs a DB query, so the cache gives limited benefit after an IDP invalidation. The resulting set is also an unordered HashSet, so result order is not preserved.

findings.title: getLoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig() and changes semantics
findings.body: The new condition treats an org-linked IDP as a login IDP only if BROKER_PUBLIC is true. This is used for cache invalidation decisions. The ORG_ONLY fetch with a specific organizationId includes the public filter, so it is consistent, but any other consumer of the predicate now behaves differently. Linking or unlinking an IDP to an org through the organization API changes the org id without going through this check unless update() is called.
